title: Evening Brief — Tue 24 Nov

stories.board: Eisenkot signs first partner; Golan walks away
stories.headline: Israel's Eisenkot wins his first coalition partner, but loses another
stories.what: Gadi Eisenkot's Yashar party agreed to a coalition deal (a deal to govern together) with Avigdor Liberman's party. On the same night, Yair Golan's Democrats stopped talks with Eisenkot because he is also talking with Netanyahu's Likud.
stories.why: Eisenkot has until about Dec 6 to form a government, and these moves decide if Israel gets a new leader or a shared one with Netanyahu.
stories.sides: Wire reports call it Eisenkot's first real deal; right-leaning Israel National News calls it an opposition crisis; Golan calls the Likud talks a sham.

stories.board: Chips sink, Dow tops 50,000, Anthropic slips
stories.headline: Tech stocks fall at the close while the Dow climbs back over 50,000
stories.what: Nvidia fell about 6 percent and the Nasdaq (mostly tech companies) fell about 1.5 percent. The Dow rose about 0.9 percent to 50,018, and new AI company Anthropic closed at 81.91 dollars, below its 83 dollar IPO price (the price when it first sold shares).
stories.why: Investors moved money out of AI chip companies and into others, which shows how jumpy people are about AI right now.
stories.sides: No major disagreement on the numbers; some right-leaning outlets say Anthropic's high costs raise doubts about AI profits, while many analysts stay positive on it.

stories.board: Nvidia boss Huang to testify Dec 3
stories.headline: Lawmakers from both parties call Nvidia's Jensen Huang to testify
stories.what: Huang is set to answer questions in public at the Senate Banking Committee on Dec. 3, and talk to three House committees. This follows his return as Nvidia boss, which Trump pushed for, after worries about his ties to a woman officials thought was a spy.
stories.why: Nvidia makes the chips that power most AI, so questions about China and national security (keeping the country safe) matter a lot.
stories.sides: Democrats like Elizabeth Warren call it reckless, and some Republicans also have questions; Trump says the board did what he wanted.

quick_hits: Canada's government has not yet answered the Pentagon's sharp complaint about Canada's military spending and F-35 jet review.
Ukraine's President Zelensky says he is ready for four-way peace talks with Russia, Europe and the US as soon as possible.
Israel's Likud and Eisenkot's party plan a third round of unity talks on Wednesday.
big_picture: Israel's next government is still up for grabs, and the AI boom is getting a bumpy ride on Wall Street and in Congress.
